newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: OAU to hold all-party talks on Comoros crisis.
newsitem.headline: OAU to hold all-party talks on Comoros crisis.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity says all parties to a secessionist crisis on the Comoro Islands have agreed to attend talks.
The OAU's Conflict Prevention, Management and Resolution (CPMR) committee said in a statement on Monday it instructed Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim to convene the talks.

"The (CPMR's) central organ welcomed the acceptance by the (Comoros) government and all the parties concerned for the holding of a conference under the OAU auspices and invites the secretary-general to take steps to convene such a conference as soon as possible," the OAU statement said.
No date or venue for the talks has been set.
Anjouan, the second largest island in the Comoros archipelago in the Indian Ocean, broke away in early August after weeks of unrest and the smallest island, Moheli, followed suit.

Islanders on Anjouan say they want to return to French rule or become independent because they have received little from the government except poverty and numerous coups since Comoran independence in 1975.
Anjouan and Moheli secessionists said last week they would meet the government at a neutral location, possibly Mauritius.
The OAU reaffirmed its "unequivocal support ... for the unity, territorial integrity and cohesion of the Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros."
It appealed to all parties to exercise maximum restraint and cooperate with the OAU initiative, and said the OAU would organise a pledging conference for international donors.
